marta: nsys trace for the kvcache perf regression run is showing anonymous addresses for CUDA kernels (no function names or source lines). lots of [0x7f9c...] entries in the timeline, can't map hotspots to our kernels. anyone seen this?

nick: yeah, usually a CUPTI / host-container lib mismatch or missing CUPTI mapping. can you paste the trace header + a snippet? also which image you ran it in (prod-perf vs dev-profiling)?

marta: ran in 'dev-profiling:latest' (our profiling image). snippet from nsys timeline:
```
CUDA API: cuLaunchKernel +0.000us (addr=0x7f9c2a1c)
GPU Kernel: 0x7f9c2a1c duration=280us
GPU Kernel: 0x7f9c2b30 duration=310us
GPU Kernel: 0x7f9c2c40 duration=120us
...
(no symbol names, no file:line)
```

sasha: quick checks: 1) does the container include libcupti.so from the same CUDA version as the host driver? 2) are the libs mounted read-only from host or built into the image? 3) confirm the build used -g/wasn't stripped for the runtime that produced the kernel symbols.

ryan: commands to run:
```
# inside container
ldd /usr/local/cuda/extras/CUPTI/lib64/libcupti.so || true
readelf -n /proc/$(pgrep -n your_app)/exe | head -n 20
nsys profile --output=kvcache --trace=cuda,kernels --force-overwrite ./run_kvcache_test
```
If ldd shows unresolved libs or points at host libs that aren't there, you'll get missing symbol resolution. Also check `readelf --notes` for build-id mismatches.

perf-bot: PERF ALERT: p99 latency +12% on kvcache serving path in the last run (build 2026-03-18-54).

nick: one subtlety: many of our profiling images don't ship CUPTI; docker runtime mounts driver libs from the host at /usr/local/nvidia/lib64 but not extras/CUPTI by default. nsys needs the libcupti that matches the host driver to resolve kernel names. If container has a different libcupti or none, you get addresses only. Try mounting host CUPTI into the container.

marta: trying that now. command I'm about to run:
```
docker run --gpus=all --rm -it \
  --volume /usr/local/cuda/extras/CUPTI:/usr/local/cuda/extras/CUPTI:ro \
  --volume /usr/local/nvidia:/usr/local/nvidia:ro \
  dev-profiling:latest /bin/bash -c "nsys profile --output=kvcache --trace=cuda,kernels ./run_kvcache_test"
```

sasha: also check for build stripping flags in our runtime Dockerfile, e.g. `-s` or `strip` steps. For kernel->source mapping you need the device side symbol information produced by the LLVM/NVCC tooling; if we compiled with device debug disabled you'll only get addresses.

marta: after mounting host CUPTI the re-run shows symbol names back in the timeline. example: `KVCache::apply_update(cuda_kernel_name)` instead of 0x7f9c2a1c. symbols restored :tada:

ryan: awesome. two follow-ups: 1) ensure the dev-profiling image documents that CUPTI must be mounted for accurate traces (or vendor a compatible lib into the image), 2) add a CI smoke that runs a short nsys profile in our profiling image and asserts that at least one kernel name is present in the output (sanity check for future regressions).

infra-bot: opened issue INF-1234: "mount CUPTI in profiling containers / CI smoke for nsys symbol resolution" with assignees sasha, marta.

nick: note for the docs/PR: also mention clock sync issues. if host/container clocks drift you may see slight timeline offsets (not our case here, but we once saw kernel timestamps off by ~1–2ms; perfetto + nsys have flags to align timestamps).

marta: creating a small runbook in /docs/internal/profiling.md with the mount example + ldd/readelf checks. will include the CI job recipe.

sasha: thanks — this explains why the perf regression couldn't be attributed to a specific kernel earlier. glad it was just symbol resolution and not an unknown kernel optimization gone wrong.

marta: marking thread resolved for now, leaving INF-1234 open for the CI + image fix. :white_check_mark:
